intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages, culminating in a breathtaking 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and surrounding Himalayan peaks. This is the crown jewel of the region and perfectly suits trekking and nature enthusiasts.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most celebrated sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Machapuchare in a spectacular alpenglow display. The hike from Ghorepani takes about 45 minutes and is accessible even for moderate hikers.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering stunning views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and Mardi Himal peak. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests teeming with wildlife, including Himalayan pheasants and langur monkeys. This off-the-beaten-path route offers solitude and raw natural beauty away from the main trekking crowds.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal Trail, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk in Ghandruk
experiences.description: Wander through Ghandruk, one of the largest and most picturesque Gurung villages in Nepal. Explore stone-paved lanes, visit the Gurung Museum to learn about indigenous culture and traditions, and interact with locals in their traditional attire. Enjoy sweeping views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli while experiencing authentic mountain village life that has remained unchanged for centuries.

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: After days of trekking, reward your tired muscles with a rejuvenating soak in the natural hot springs along the Modi River at Jhinu Danda. These geothermal pools sit beside a rushing glacial river surrounded by lush forest, offering a uniquely restorative nature experience. The 20-minute downhill hike from Jhinu village adds a final mini-adventure before you unwind completely.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or shared shuttle to your accommodation near the Annapurna region (or overnight stay near Pokhara if transfer is needed). Check in and rest.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick dal bhat or noodle soup at a local teahouse near the airport area if arriving early enough — approx $2–4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Keep USD or NPR cash ready for taxi and tips. Exchange some currency at the airport. Confirm hotel booking. Dress in layers — October nights in Annapurna region can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and acclimatize after long travel. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Take a short orientation walk around the local village near your accommodation to get familiar with the surroundings and nearby trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local Pokhara lakeside area (Phewa Lake) if staying near Pokhara. Stroll along the lakeside promenade, browse local trekking gear shops for any budget supplies needed, and visit the Bindhyabasini Temple — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside Bazaar for budget souvenir shopping. Enjoy dinner at a local daal bhaat restaurant along the main street.

meals.breakfast: Dal bhat or eggs with tea at resort or local teahouse — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and lemon tea at a local café — approx $2–3 USD
meals.dinner: Traditional Nepali dal bhat thali at a local restaurant — approx $3–5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Buy or rent trekking poles, warm layers, and a good sleeping bag liner if needed from Lakeside shops — prices are very negotiable. Stay hydrated and rest well for upcoming treks.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple (island temple) — boat hire approx $3–5 USD round trip. Enjoy the stunning Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) mountain reflections on the lake at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a local bus to Nayapul (approx $2 USD by local bus) — the starting point of the Annapurna Base Camp or Poon Hill trek. Begin the first leg of the trek to Tikhedhunga (1,540m), a moderate 2–3 hour walk through terraced fields and small villages.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga. Check into a budget teahouse (approx $3–6 USD per night). Relax, enjoy the mountain views, and socialize with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with chapati at resort — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or noodle soup at a trail-side teahouse — approx $2–4 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Tikhedhunga teahouse — approx $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Obtain your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card before departure — approx $30–35 USD total. Start trekking early to avoid afternoon heat. Carry at least 2 liters of water.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Tikhedhunga. Trek up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m) — a steep but rewarding 1.5-hour climb with panoramic views. Continue through rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani after approximately 5–6 hours total trekking. Check into a budget teahouse. Rest and explore the small village. Visit the local viewpoint for first glimpses of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up by the communal fire at the teahouse. Chat with fellow trekkers and plan the early morning Poon Hill sunrise hike. Early bedtime recommended.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and black tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Veggie fried rice or noodle soup at a trail teahouse — approx $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse — approx $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: The climb to Ulleri has over 3,000 stone steps — pace yourself and take regular breaks. Temperatures drop significantly at Ghorepani — have warm layers ready. Set alarm for 04:30 AM for Poon Hill sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:30 AM. Trek 45 minutes by torchlight to Poon Hill (3,210m) for the iconic sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges — one of Nepal's most spectacular viewpoints. Entry fee approx $2 USD. Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani through dense rhododendron forest to Tadapani (2,630m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail offers beautiful forest scenery and occasional mountain views through the canopy.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani. Check into teahouse. Enjoy the peaceful forested setting and clear evening mountain views. Rest your legs.

meals.breakfast: Hot lemon tea on Poon Hill, then eggs and toast at teahouse after descent — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and chapati at a trail teahouse — approx $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse — approx $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the trek — arrive early to secure a good viewpoint spot. The forest trail to Tadapani can be muddy in October — trekking poles are very helpful. Carry snacks like nuts and energy bars.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours through beautiful mixed forest with views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. The trail involves some steep descents and ascents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong — a picturesque Gurung village. Explore the village, visit the local monastery, and enjoy stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from the village viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse. Chhomrong has slightly better facilities than previous stops — enjoy a hot shower if available (approx $1–2 USD extra). Prepare gear for the higher altitude sections ahead.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with milk and tea at Tadapani — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Pasta or fried noodles at a trail teahouse — approx $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (good for altitude) and dal bhat at Chhomrong teahouse — approx $5–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is the last major village before the higher altitude zones. Stock up on snacks and water purification tablets. Prices increase slightly at higher elevations. Garlic soup is highly recommended for altitude acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong through Sinuwa (2,360m) and into the beautiful bamboo and rhododendron forest to Dovan (2,600m) — approximately 5–6 hours. The trail enters the dramatic Modi Khola gorge with towering canyon walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking if energy allows, or rest at Dovan teahouse. Short afternoon walk along the river gorge to enjoy the dramatic scenery and waterfalls. The sound of the Modi Khola river is incredibly soothing.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Dovan teahouse. The gorge creates a unique microclimate — evenings can be misty and atmospheric. Early dinner and rest for the big push to Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Chhomrong — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Instant noodles or soup at Bamboo teahouse — approx $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse — approx $5–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: The bamboo forest section is magical but can be slippery — walk carefully. Leeches may be present in lower sections after rain — tuck trousers into socks. Temperatures are dropping — ensure sleeping bag is rated to at least -5°C.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — approximately 4–5 hours via Himalaya Hotel and Deurali. The trail becomes more open with dramatic views of the surrounding peaks and glacial moraines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approximately 1.5–2 hours. Arrive at ABC and soak in the extraordinary 360-degree amphitheater of Himalayan giants including Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate reaching ABC! Watch the alpenglow turn the peaks golden at sunset. This is the crown jewel of the entire trek. Spend the evening in awe of the surrounding mountains.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at Dovan — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at Machhapuchhre Base Camp teahouse — approx $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pizza (yes, they make it here!) at ABC teahouse — approx $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real risk at ABC — move slowly, drink plenty of water, and descend immediately if you experience severe headache, vomiting, or confusion. Temperatures at ABC can drop to -10°C at night in October. Prices at ABC are higher due to porter transport costs.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn at ABC for the magical sunrise over the Annapurna Sanctuary — the mountains turn vivid shades of pink, orange, and gold. Spend the morning exploring around the base camp, taking photos, and absorbing the incredible atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back to Bamboo (2,310m) — approximately 5–6 hours descending via MBC and Deurali. The descent is faster but hard on the knees — use trekking poles.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse. Enjoy the warmer, lower altitude air. Celebrate your successful ABC summit with fellow trekkers over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at ABC — approx $4–5 USD
meals.lunch: Soup and snacks at MBC or Deurali teahouse — approx $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra portions at Bamboo teahouse — approx $5–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Descending is easier but puts significant strain on knees — trekking poles are essential. Take your time and enjoy the views you may have missed on the way up. Stay hydrated even while descending.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back to Chhomrong — approximately 4–5 hours. Enjoy the reverse perspective of the trail through the bamboo forest and back up to the Gurung village. Legs will be tired but spirits will be high.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest afternoon in Chhomrong. Take a well-deserved hot shower. Visit the local Gurung Cultural Museum if available, or simply relax and enjoy the views with a cup of masala chai.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a celebratory dinner at one of Chhomrong's slightly better-equipped teahouses. Share stories with other returning trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and chapati at Bamboo — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at a trail teahouse — approx $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Special mixed plate — dal bhat, vegetable curry, and pickle at Chhomrong — approx $5–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Your body will be fatigued after the high-altitude push — rest well. Check your feet for blisters and treat them. Refill water bottles and restock snacks for the final descent days.

day_by_day.morning: Final descent from Chhomrong through Jhinu Danda (1,780m). Jhinu Danda has a famous natural hot spring along the Modi Khola river — a perfect reward for tired trekking legs. Trek takes approximately 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs for 1–2 hours — entry fee approx $2–3 USD. This is one of the most rewarding experiences after days of trekking. Continue trekking to Nayapul and take a local bus or jeep back to Pokhara.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pokhara/resort area. Check back into accommodation. Enjoy a proper shower, comfortable bed, and the luxury of being back at lower altitude.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Chhomrong — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Jhinu Danda teahouse — approx $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Celebrate your trek completion with a slightly splurge-worthy dinner at a Lakeside restaurant — momos, thukpa, and lassi — approx $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Don't miss the hot springs — they are genuinely therapeutic after 9 days of trekking. Local bus from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approx $1.50–2 USD. Jeep is faster at approx $4–6 USD per person shared.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — entry approx $5 USD — to learn about the history of Himalayan mountaineering and the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a peaceful rowboat on Phewa Lake — hire a local wooden boat for approx $3–5 USD per hour. Row to a quiet cove for swimming or simply enjoy the mountain reflections. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the hill above the lake — hike up for free or pay approx $1–2 USD for a boat across.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside area in the evening. Browse the colorful market stalls, pick up handmade souvenirs like pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, or carved wooden items at negotiated prices.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit bowl, yogurt, and coffee at a lakeside café — approx $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Newari set meal at a local cultural restaurant — approx $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Tibetan thukpa (noodle soup) and butter tea at a Tibetan restaurant — approx $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Your muscles will be sore — a budget massage on Lakeside costs approx $8–12 USD for 60 minutes and is highly recommended. Laundry services available on Lakeside for approx $1–2 USD per kg.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Sarangkot Hill (1,592m) — a 2–3 hour hike from Pokhara offering arguably the best panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Start early for clear skies. The hike is free and the views are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Sarangkot and visit the Devi's Fall (Patale Chhango) — entry approx $2 USD — a dramatic waterfall that disappears underground. Walk across to the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave directly opposite — entry approx $2 USD — a sacred Hindu cave with underground river.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Annapurna/Pokhara region. Take one last sunset walk along the Phewa Lake promenade. Reflect on the incredible trek and natural beauty experienced over the past two weeks.

meals.breakfast: Egg sandwiches and tea packed for the Sarangkot hike — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a local Sarangkot village restaurant — approx $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — mixed Nepali-Continental menu at a budget lakeside restaurant — approx $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot is also famous for paragliding (approx $70–90 USD) if budget allows for a splurge — one of the world's top paragliding destinations. Pack your bags tonight for early morning departure. Keep important documents accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final walk along Phewa Lake at sunrise — a peaceful and beautiful farewell to the Annapurna region. Pack remaining belongings. Check out of accommodation. Arrange budget taxi or tourist bus to Kathmandu (approx $8–12 USD by tourist bus, 6–7 hours) or domestic flight (approx $80–100 USD, 25 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: If taking the bus to Kathmandu, enjoy the scenic Prithvi Highway journey through river gorges and terraced hillsides. If arriving in Kathmandu early, visit Thamel neighborhood for last-minute shopping and exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu. Transfer to airport area accommodation or directly to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. Final dinner of authentic Nepali food before heading home.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast — sel roti (rice doughnut), yogurt, and tea — approx $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or stop at a roadside dhaba — dal bhat — approx $2–4 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell Nepali thali at a Thamel restaurant — approx $4–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for check-in and security. Keep $25 USD cash for Nepal departure tax if not included in ticket. Take one last look at the Himalayas from the plane window — on clear days the views of Everest and Annapurna from the aircraft are breathtaking.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to your accommodation near Pokhara/Annapurna region. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service upon arrival if available at the resort

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival at 22:30, plan for minimal activity tonight. Confirm your transfer in advance. Keep snacks handy for the journey. Rest well — acclimatization begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy breakfast at the resort and take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeside area (Phewa Lake if near Pokhara). Breathe in the fresh Himalayan air and get your first views of the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pokhara Lakeside bazaar for a relaxed stroll. Browse local handicraft shops, pick up trekking essentials if needed, and visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara and the Annapurna massif. Light hike up to the stupa takes about 45 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lakeside area. Explore the vibrant Lakeside street for dinner. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere with mountain views at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — try local sel roti with tea or eggs and toast
meals.lunch: Momos and thukpa at a local Lakeside café (budget-friendly, ~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at a mid-range Nepali restaurant like Lemon Tree or Beam Beam Restaurant (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light for acclimatization and orientation. Pokhara sits at ~820m elevation. Stay hydrated and avoid alcohol on your first full day. Confirm trekking permits and gear for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat ride on Phewa Lake at sunrise — a magical experience with mirror reflections of Machhapuchhre (Fish Tail Mountain) and the Annapurna range. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple located on an island in the lake. Boats available from the lakeside (~$3–5 USD for an hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a local bus to Nayapul (about 1.5 hours from Pokhara) and begin the introductory hike toward Tikhedhunga or Hile. This is the classic start of the Annapurna Circuit/Poon Hill trail. Walk through terraced rice fields, traditional Gurung villages, and lush subtropical forests. Distance: ~8–10 km, 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in at a comfortable teahouse in Tikhedhunga or Hile. Relax on the teahouse porch with views of the surrounding hills. Socialize with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — porridge, eggs, toast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or dal bhat at a local teahouse along the trail (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner: vegetable curry, rice, lentil soup (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card before departing Pokhara if not already done. Cost: ~$30–35 USD total. Tikhedhunga sits at ~1,540m — a gentle start to trekking altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and begin the iconic climb from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani via Ulleri. The steep stone staircase up to Ulleri (3,280 stone steps!) is challenging but incredibly rewarding. Pass through rhododendron and oak forests. Distance: ~11 km, 5–6 hours total to Ghorepani.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through dense rhododendron forests toward Ghorepani (2,874m). Arrive in the afternoon and check into a mid-range teahouse. Rest, stretch, and hydrate. Explore the small village and enjoy the first high-altitude mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges golden from Ghorepani. Warm up with a cup of ginger lemon honey tea. Chat with other trekkers and rest for the big Poon Hill sunrise tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast: porridge or pancakes with honey and tea
meals.lunch: Lunch break on trail: noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Ghorepani teahouse (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most physically demanding days of the trip. Start early (6:30–7:00 AM). Pace yourself on the Ulleri stairs. Ghorepani elevation is 2,874m — watch for signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea). Drink 3–4 liters of water throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM for the iconic Poon Hill sunrise hike (3,210m). A 45-minute uphill walk in the dark (bring headlamp) rewards you with one of the most spectacular sunrise panoramas in the Himalayas — Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and more. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani through stunning rhododendron forests. The trail offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife. Distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) and check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Tadapani with unobstructed views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South. Write in your journal, review photos, and rest your legs. Early bedtime recommended.

meals.breakfast: Post-Poon Hill breakfast at Ghorepani teahouse: eggs, toast, porridge
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodles at a teahouse along the Tadapani trail (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and soup at Tadapani teahouse (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Poon Hill sunrise is the highlight of many Annapurna treks — do not miss it. Bring warm layers for the pre-dawn hike (temperatures can drop to 0–5°C in October). The trail to Tadapani has some steep sections — trekking poles recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m), a beautiful Gurung village with terraced fields and panoramic Annapurna views. The trail descends steeply before climbing again. Distance: ~9 km, 4–5 hours. Chhomrong is the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into a well-equipped teahouse. Explore the village — visit the local bakery (famous in trekking circles!), browse the small shops, and admire the stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing evening in Chhomrong. The village has some of the best-equipped teahouses on this route with hot showers available. Treat yourself to a warm shower (~$2–3 USD extra) and a cozy dinner.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani teahouse: pancakes or muesli with fruit
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or quick stop at a trail teahouse: apple pie and tea
meals.dinner: Chhomrong teahouse: garlic soup (great for altitude), pasta, or dal bhat (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is highly recommended at altitude — locals and trekkers swear by its acclimatization benefits. Chhomrong has reliable WiFi at some teahouses. This is a good point to assess your fitness and decide whether to continue toward Annapurna Base Camp.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down to Sinuwa and then through the bamboo and rhododendron forest to Dovan (2,600m). The trail enters the Modi Khola gorge — dramatic and increasingly wild. Distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. The forest is home to Himalayan pheasants, langur monkeys, and diverse flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) if energy permits, or rest at Dovan. The landscape becomes increasingly alpine with towering canyon walls. Afternoon clouds often roll in — enjoy the dramatic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse at Himalaya Hotel or Dovan. The remoteness here is palpable — you're deep in the Annapurna Sanctuary approach. Enjoy stargazing if skies are clear — the Milky Way is spectacular at this elevation.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong teahouse: eggs, toast, hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Sinuwa or Dovan: fried rice or noodle soup (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner: dal bhat, vegetable curry, or pasta (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — teahouses can be busy. Book ahead or arrive early to secure rooms. Leeches are less common in October but carry salt just in case. The gorge can be cold and damp — waterproof layers essential.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Himalaya Hotel to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. The trail opens up dramatically into a glacial amphitheater. Pass through Hinku Cave and Deurali. The views of Machhapuchhre (Fish Tail) looming above are awe-inspiring. Distance: ~8 km, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: From MBC, continue the final push to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — the crown jewel of this trek. Surrounded by a 360° panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna. Arrive and soak in the majesty.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from ABC — the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks is otherworldly. Celebrate reaching base camp with fellow trekkers. Rest well and stay warm — temperatures drop significantly at night.

meals.breakfast: Early teahouse breakfast: porridge, eggs, hot tea
meals.lunch: Quick snack at MBC teahouse: biscuits, chocolate, hot lemon tea
meals.dinner: ABC teahouse: dal bhat or pasta — hearty meal after a major achievement (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Watch carefully for altitude sickness symptoms: severe headache, vomiting, loss of coordination. If symptoms worsen, descend immediately. Acclimatization days in lower camps help significantly. Nights at ABC are very cold — sleeping bag rated to -10°C recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise at ABC for the most spectacular mountain sunrise of your life — the entire Annapurna massif turns shades of pink, orange, and gold. Spend the morning exploring around base camp, taking photos, and absorbing the high-altitude environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back toward Chhomrong. The descent is faster — aim to reach Bamboo or Sinuwa. Distance: ~16–18 km descending, 5–6 hours. Legs will feel the downhill — take it steady on knees.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse. Celebrate the successful ABC summit with a slice of apple pie (a trekking trail tradition!) and a well-earned rest.

meals.breakfast: ABC teahouse: porridge and hot tea before sunrise, proper breakfast after
meals.lunch: Snack on trail: energy bars, nuts, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Bamboo/Sinuwa teahouse: dal bhat, vegetable noodles, or egg fried rice (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Descent days are hard on knees — use trekking poles and take your time. You've completed the main trekking highlight of the trip! Stay hydrated even on descent. The trail can be slippery in morning frost — be cautious.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Sinuwa/Bamboo back through Chhomrong and down to Jhinu Danda (1,780m). Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs located a short 20-minute walk below the village on the river bank.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a glorious afternoon soaking in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs — the perfect reward after days of trekking. The warm mineral waters overlooking the Modi Khola river are pure bliss for tired muscles. Soak for 1–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jhinu Danda teahouse for the night. Enjoy a relaxed evening — legs feel rejuvenated after the hot springs. Early rest in preparation for the final trekking days.

meals.breakfast: Sinuwa/Bamboo teahouse: pancakes, eggs, tea
meals.lunch: Chhomrong village bakery stop: cinnamon roll, coffee, apple pie (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Jhinu Danda teahouse: dal bhat or pasta with local vegetable curry (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a beloved trekking tradition on this route. Entry fee is minimal (~$1–2 USD). The springs are open-air by the river — bring a towel and change of clothes. This is one of the most memorable and restorative stops of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day — descend from Jhinu Danda through Landruk and down to the road head at Kimche or Nayapul. The trail passes through beautiful Gurung villages with traditional stone houses and terraced fields. Distance: ~10–12 km, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a local jeep or bus back to Pokhara (1–1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort and check back in. Take a long, hot shower and change into clean clothes — one of the greatest feelings after a trek!
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your Annapurna trek with a proper dinner in Pokhara's Lakeside district. Enjoy the lively atmosphere, live music, and well-deserved comfort food.

meals.breakfast: Jhinu Danda teahouse: oatmeal, eggs, hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Village teahouse lunch near Landruk: dal bhat or noodle soup (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a Lakeside restaurant — try Moondance Restaurant or Lemon Tree for a mix of Nepali and international cuisine (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: You've completed approximately 8 days of trekking covering 100+ km and reaching 4,130m elevation — a major achievement! Treat yourself tonight. The Lakeside area has great restaurants, cafés, and bars for a celebratory evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast, and take a gentle walk along Phewa Lake. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — an excellent museum dedicated to the Himalayas, mountaineering history, and local cultures (~$5 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activity: try paragliding over Pokhara from Sarangkot — one of the world's best paragliding locations with views of the Annapurna range ($70–90 USD for a tandem flight, 30–45 minutes). Alternatively, rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake for a peaceful paddle.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Sarangkot viewpoint (if not already visited) or from Lakeside. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and browse souvenir shops for gifts — Pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, lokta paper products, and hand-knit goods are excellent buys.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: full spread — eggs, toast, fruit, juice, coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside café: pizza, pasta, or a sandwich (~$6–9 USD) — a treat after trail food
meals.dinner: Nepali thali dinner at a local restaurant: full set with rice, curries, pickles, papad (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding in Pokhara is world-class and safe with reputable operators. Book through your resort or a licensed operator. October weather is generally excellent for paragliding — clear skies and stable thermals. Rest your legs today — they deserve it!

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Annapurna foothills: visit the Australian Camp and Kande area for a short scenic hike (2–3 hours) with stunning views of the Annapurna range. Much easier than the main trek — perfect for tired legs. Alternatively, visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls near Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bindhyabasini Temple — one of Pokhara's most important Hindu temples set on a hilltop with city and mountain views. Then explore the Old Pokhara Bazaar area (Bagar) for authentic local market culture, traditional architecture, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Annapurna region. Enjoy a sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake and dinner at a rooftop restaurant with mountain views. Reflect on the incredible journey of the past two weeks.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café: sel roti with yogurt and honey — traditional Nepali breakfast
meals.lunch: Old Bazaar street food: samosas, chow mein, fresh fruit (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant dinner: mix of Nepali and continental — try yak cheese pizza or butter chicken (~$10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave are within 2 km of Lakeside — easy to visit by foot or rickshaw. The Old Bazaar gives an authentic glimpse of traditional Pokhara life away from the tourist strip. Pack your bags tonight for departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from the resort or lakeside. Take a final peaceful walk along Phewa Lake and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Complete any last-minute souvenir shopping in Lakeside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange transfer back to Kathmandu (either by tourist bus ~8 hours, or domestic flight ~25 minutes — flight recommended for time efficiency). If time permits in Kathmandu, visit Thamel for last-minute shopping or a quick visit to Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu for departure. Depart Nepal with incredible memories of the Annapurna region, Himalayan sunrises, and the warmth of the Nepali people.

meals.breakfast: Resort farewell breakfast: full spread with coffee — savor the mountain views one last time
meals.lunch: Airport or Thamel restaurant: final dal bhat or momo meal (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Book your Pokhara-Kathmandu domestic flight in advance (Buddha Air or Yeti Airlines, ~$100–120 USD one way) — much faster than the bus. Arrive at Kathmandu airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Nepal departure tax is typically included in your ticket. Carry trekking memories, not just souvenirs!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most celebrated sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Machapuchare in a spectacular alpenglow display. The hike from Ghorepani takes about 45 minutes and is accessible even for moderate hikers.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport at 22:30 — No morning activities scheduled due to late-night arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Annapurna. Upon arrival, enjoy a warm welcome with traditional Nepali tea and a light late-night refreshment platter prepared by the resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining.
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day.
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated selection of local cheeses, seasonal fruits, Nepali sel roti, and herbal teas served in-room.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Porter and concierge will handle all luggage. Hydrate well upon arrival as altitude acclimatization begins immediately. Resort elevation briefing packet will be left in your suite.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a gourmet Nepali and continental breakfast at the resort's panoramic dining terrace overlooking the Annapurna range. After breakfast, meet with your dedicated private trekking guide for a full trip orientation, gear check, and acclimatization briefing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introductory nature walk around the resort's immediate surroundings — explore local flora, terraced farmlands, and nearby riverside trails at low elevation. This easy 2–3 hour stroll is designed to begin acclimatization without physical strain. Visit a nearby traditional Gurung village for a cultural introduction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private terrace with unobstructed Annapurna massif views. Enjoy a curated welcome dinner featuring authentic Newari cuisine prepared by the resort's executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet Nepali and continental breakfast at the resort terrace — eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, Nepali dhido, seasonal fruits, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Light farm-to-table lunch at the resort — grilled mountain vegetables, lentil soup, and freshly baked Tibetan bread.
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — Newari-inspired tasting menu with paired local craft beverages and Himalayan herbal digestifs.

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization is critical on Day 2. Avoid strenuous activity. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. The guide will review the full 14-day itinerary and make any adjustments based on your fitness level and weather conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the classic Annapurna foothills trek — private guided hike from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, moderate terrain). Walk through lush subtropical forests, cross suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river, and pass through charming Magar villages. Enjoy the dramatic shift in landscape as you gain elevation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Ulleri (1,960m) — a challenging but rewarding stone-staircase ascent through rhododendron forests. Arrive at a premium teahouse lodge pre-booked exclusively for your party. Rest, freshen up with hot water provided, and enjoy the sweeping valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the Ulleri hillside. Private chef-prepared dinner at your exclusive teahouse lodge. Stargazing session with the guide — at this elevation, the Milky Way is clearly visible on clear October nights.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the resort before departure — porridge, eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the resort chef — artisan sandwiches, energy bars, seasonal fruit, and thermos of hot soup.
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner — dal bhat thali with organic vegetables, locally sourced grilled chicken, and Himalayan herbal tea.

day_by_day.notes: Porter service included — you carry only a light daypack. Trek distance: approximately 12–14 km. Trekking poles recommended. Weather in October is typically clear and cool — ideal trekking conditions. Ensure all gear is packed the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860m) through magnificent rhododendron and oak forests — one of the most scenic forest treks in the Annapurna region. The trail offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife. Arrive at Ghorepani by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your premium lodge in Ghorepani. Rest and acclimatize. Afternoon optional short hike to a nearby viewpoint for a preview of the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges. Visit the local market and interact with Gurung and Magar community members.
day_by_day.evening: Private guided sunset walk on the ridge above Ghorepani. Return for a warm dinner and early bedtime in preparation for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike tomorrow morning.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Ulleri teahouse — pancakes, eggs, Tibetan bread with honey, and ginger tea.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the trail — enjoyed at a scenic rest stop with mountain views.
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner at Ghorepani — hearty mountain cuisine including yak cheese soup, vegetable curry, rice, and warm apple cider.

day_by_day.notes: Set alarms for 04:00 AM tomorrow for the Poon Hill sunrise hike. The lodge will prepare packed hot drinks and light snacks for the early morning ascent. Temperatures at Ghorepani can drop to 2–5°C at night in October — ensure thermal layers are accessible.

day_by_day.morning: PRE-DAWN POON HILL SUNRISE HIKE — Wake at 04:00 AM. Guided hike by headlamp to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m), approximately 45 minutes from Ghorepani. Witness one of the most celebrated Himalayan sunrises, with panoramic views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Annapurna I (8,091m) bathed in golden alpenglow. Photography session with your guide. Return to lodge for a full hot breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend via the scenic Tadapani trail through dense rhododendron forests — one of the richest biodiversity corridors in the Annapurna Conservation Area. Arrive at Tadapani (2,590m) for a well-earned lunch and rest. Optional nature walk to a nearby waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your premium Tadapani lodge. Enjoy a peaceful evening with valley views, followed by a private candlelit dinner. Reflection journaling time encouraged — your guide will share stories of Himalayan culture and mythology.

meals.breakfast: Hot drinks (ginger tea, hot chocolate) before Poon Hill ascent. Full hot breakfast upon return — eggs, porridge, pancakes, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Tadapani lodge — lentil soup, vegetable momos, rice, and seasonal pickles.
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at Tadapani lodge — chef-prepared Nepali set meal with organic produce, followed by warm cinnamon apple dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the Annapurna foothills circuit. October skies are typically crystal clear — optimal for photography. Bring a camera with wide-angle lens. The sunrise experience is genuinely world-class and worth every early morning effort.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) — a moderately challenging trail descending through apple orchards and then ascending through terraced fields. Chhomrong is a beautiful Gurung village and the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre throughout the morning hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong and check into your premium lodge. Afternoon at leisure — explore the village, visit the local monastery, and enjoy a traditional Gurung cultural interaction arranged by your guide. Optional yoga or stretching session on the lodge terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from Chhomrong's famous ridge — arguably the best close-up view of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m). Private dinner at lodge with locally brewed raksi (millet wine) tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Tadapani — eggs, toast, porridge, and Nepali milk tea.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the trail — enjoyed at a scenic stone rest platform overlooking the Modi Khola gorge.
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner at Chhomrong — grilled mountain trout, vegetable curry, fresh rice, and traditional Gurung dessert with local honey.

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong marks the transition from the foothills to the Annapurna Sanctuary approach. Your guide will brief you on the next phase of the trek. Stock up on any personal supplies here as options become limited higher up.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Dovan (2,600m) through the spectacular bamboo and rhododendron forests of the Annapurna Sanctuary approach. Cross the famous Chhomrong Khola and begin ascending through increasingly dramatic mountain terrain. The forest is alive with Himalayan wildlife — watch for langur monkeys, Himalayan tahr, and diverse birdlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Himalaya Hotel (2,900m) or push on to Dovan depending on pace. The valley narrows dramatically as towering peaks close in on both sides — an awe-inspiring natural amphitheater. Arrive at your premium teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: The evening atmosphere in this deep valley is extraordinarily serene. Dinner by lantern light at the teahouse. Early rest in preparation for continued ascent tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Chhomrong lodge — porridge, eggs, Tibetan bread, and ginger lemon honey tea.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the trail — thermos of hot soup, sandwiches, energy snacks, and seasonal fruit.
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner — hearty dal bhat, vegetable curry, and unlimited Himalayan herbal tea to aid acclimatization.

day_by_day.notes: Altitude increases significantly today. Drink minimum 4 liters of water. Avoid alcohol. Walk at a slow, steady pace — 'Bistari bistari' (slowly slowly) is the Nepali trekking mantra. Report any headaches or nausea to your guide immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — the dramatic final approach into the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail passes through Hinku Cave and Deurali, with the valley walls rising thousands of meters on either side. The first sight of the Annapurna Sanctuary opening up is a genuinely breathtaking moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700m). Rest and acclimatize. Short exploratory walk around MBC to adjust to altitude. The views of Machhapuchhre's iconic twin-summit spire from here are extraordinary and unlike any other vantage point.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from MBC with Machhapuchhre, Annapurna III, and Gangapurna glowing in alpenglow. Private premium teahouse dinner. Stargazing at 3,700m — on clear October nights, the sky is overwhelmingly brilliant.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Dovan — eggs, porridge, toast, and multiple cups of hot tea.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — hot soup thermos, energy bars, nuts, and dried fruit.
meals.dinner: Premium MBC teahouse dinner — garlic soup (essential for altitude), vegetable pasta, rice, and hot chocolate.

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases significantly above 3,500m. Garlic soup is a traditional Himalayan remedy for altitude symptoms. Ensure Diamox is available if prescribed. Sleep at MBC tonight to properly acclimatize before ascending to Annapurna Base Camp tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: The crown jewel of the trek — hike from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m. The 2-hour ascent through glacial moraine and high-altitude meadows culminates in one of the world's most dramatic mountain amphitheaters. You are surrounded 360° by 7,000–8,000m peaks: Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. A profound, life-changing moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon at Annapurna Base Camp. Explore the base camp area, photograph the glacier, and absorb the extraordinary mountain environment. Your private guide will share the mountaineering history of these peaks — Annapurna I was the first 8,000m peak ever summited (1950, French expedition).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — the golden hour light on the surrounding peaks is indescribably beautiful. Private premium dinner at ABC lodge. Reflection and journaling. This is the highest and most remote point of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at MBC before ascent — porridge, eggs, toast, and multiple hot teas.
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at ABC upon arrival — garlic soup, noodles, and hot drinks.
meals.dinner: Premium ABC lodge dinner — hearty mountain meal with dal bhat, vegetable curry, and warm apple pie with custard.

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m is the highest point of this itinerary. Cold temperatures are expected — October nights at ABC can drop to -10°C or below. Ensure all cold-weather gear is packed in your daypack. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience — take time to fully absorb the surroundings.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp — the most spectacular sunrise of the entire trip. The first light striking Annapurna I's summit creates an otherworldly pink and gold spectacle. After a full sunrise experience and photography session, begin the descent from ABC to MBC and continue down to Bamboo (2,310m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending through the bamboo and rhododendron forest zone. The descent is rapid compared to the ascent — the body moves more easily going downhill. Arrive at Bamboo teahouse by mid-afternoon. Rest and enjoy the warmer temperatures.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Bamboo — the contrast with the high-altitude cold of ABC is immediately noticeable and welcome. Warm dinner and a full night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Hot drinks before sunrise, full hot breakfast at ABC before descent — eggs, porridge, and hot tea.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on trail or warm lunch at MBC teahouse.
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Bamboo — dal bhat, seasonal vegetables, and freshly made local bread.

day_by_day.notes: Descending from high altitude brings rapid recovery from any altitude effects. Knees and quads will feel the downhill — trekking poles strongly recommended. The descent from ABC to Bamboo covers significant elevation loss in one day — take it steadily.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day — descend from Bamboo through Sinuwa and Chhomrong, then continue down to Jhinu Danda (1,780m). This charming village is famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. Arrive by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: REWARD: Private natural hot spring session at Jhinu Danda. Soak in the geothermal pools beside the rushing river — an extraordinarily therapeutic experience after 9 days of trekking. Premium towels and changing facilities arranged in advance. This is one of Nepal's finest natural spa experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer by private vehicle from Jhinu Danda/Nayapul to your resort accommodation. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort, Annapurna. Luxurious check-in, hot shower, and a celebratory dinner to mark the completion of the Annapurna trek.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Bamboo teahouse — eggs, porridge, and ginger tea.
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Jhinu Danda teahouse — dal bhat and local seasonal vegetables.
meals.dinner: Celebratory gourmet dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — premium tasting menu with Himalayan-inspired dishes, fine wine selection, and dessert platter.

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a legendary reward for Annapurna trekkers. Water temperature is naturally warm year-round. The return to resort luxury after days of teahouse accommodation will feel extraordinarily indulgent — enjoy every moment.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast, and indulge in the resort's spa facilities — book a traditional Ayurvedic massage, hot stone therapy, or a full Himalayan herb body treatment to restore muscles after the trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Private guided nature walk through the resort's surrounding forest and river trails — a gentle, low-elevation stroll to appreciate the Annapurna foothills landscape without the demands of trekking. Alternatively, enjoy the resort pool, read, or simply rest on your private terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort bar. Private chef's table dinner experience — watch the executive chef prepare a bespoke 5-course Nepali fusion meal at your table using locally sourced organic ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at leisure — full spread of continental and Nepali options, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled fish, salads, fresh fruit platters, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Private chef's table 5-course dinner — Nepali fusion tasting menu with wine pairing and Himalayan herbal digestif.

day_by_day.notes: Day 12 is intentionally unstructured for recovery and luxury indulgence. Spa bookings should be made the evening before. The body needs 24–48 hours of rest after a high-altitude multi-day trek. Hydration remains important.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise helicopter flight over the Annapurna massif — the ultimate luxury Himalayan experience. A private helicopter departs from the nearest helipad and provides a 60–90 minute aerial tour of Annapurna I, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and the Annapurna Sanctuary from above. Land briefly at a high-altitude viewpoint for a champagne toast in the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by late morning. Afternoon cultural excursion — private guided visit to Pokhara city (approximately 1–2 hours from the resort). Explore the lakeside promenade of Phewa Lake, visit the International Mountain Museum, and browse artisan shops for authentic Nepali crafts, thangka paintings, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake with Annapurna range reflections on the water — a magical and iconic Nepali experience. Dinner at one of Pokhara's finest lakeside restaurants before private transfer back to resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort before helicopter departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant — fresh lake fish, Nepali thali, and local craft beer.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a top Pokhara lakeside restaurant — international and Nepali fusion cuisine with Phewa Lake views.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are subject to weather conditions — October is generally excellent for flying. Book helicopter in advance and confirm the morning of. The aerial perspective of the Annapurna range is dramatically different from and complementary to the ground-level trekking experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up for one last sunrise over the Annapurna range from your private terrace. Leisurely final breakfast. Pack and prepare for departure. Final meeting with your guide to exchange contacts, receive a personalized trekking certificate, and share memories of the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Pokhara Airport or Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, depending on departure flight. En route, stop at a premium artisan shop for final souvenir purchases — handmade pashmina, lokta paper journals, and Himalayan tea collections.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nepal. Carry with you the memories of Poon Hill sunrises, Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, natural hot springs, helicopter views, and the profound warmth of Nepali hospitality. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread with all favorites from the past two weeks.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pokhara or airport lounge — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juice.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and airport transfer timing the evening before. Allow extra time for airport procedures in Nepal. Ensure all trekking permits, receipts, and documentation are collected as souvenirs. Tip your guide, porters, and resort staff generously — it makes a meaningful difference to local communities.
